I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII domain names when using non-Unicode email encodings:

- Added [`punycode()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xd8fzyvk/django/utils/encoding.py#L251-L253) in [django/utils/encoding.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xd8fzyvk/django/utils/encoding.py) to convert non-ASCII domain names to Punycode (`domain.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`), and updated existing IDNA domain conversions in [django/core/mail/message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xd8fzyvk/django/core/mail/message.py), [django/core/validators.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xd8fzyvk/django/core/validators.py), and [django/utils/html.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xd8fzyvk/django/utils/html.py) to use it.
- Updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xd8fzyvk/django/core/mail/utils.py#L15-L18) in [django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xd8fzyvk/django/core/mail/utils.py) to convert the FQDN returned by `socket.getfqdn()` to Punycode.
